hits.tldr: Theme variables compile to CSS custom properties for use in stylesheets.
Tailwind CSS imports default theme variables for colors, fonts, shadows, and spacing via layer declarations.
Use the prefix option to namespace Tailwind CSS classes and variables to avoid naming conflicts.
Prefixed classes appear at the start of class names, theme variables are configured without prefix but generated CSS includes it.
Use the `inline` option when theme variables reference other variables to avoid CSS resolution issues.

hits.tldr: Tailwind CSS imports default theme variables for colors, fonts, shadows, and spacing via layer declarations.
Theme variables in Tailwind's `--font-*` namespace automatically generate corresponding font utility classes.
Use the prefix option to namespace Tailwind CSS classes and variables to avoid naming conflicts.
Override default theme variables by redefining them in @theme or reset entire namespaces with asterisk syntax.
Set the theme namespace to `initial` to disable default values and use only custom theme variables.

content.text:
No, it isn't safe. Unprefixed `--color-*` variables in `:root` can collide with your users' own variables. The docs don't mention that risk explicitly, but they do give a fix.

- **Fix:** use `@import "tailwindcss" prefix(tw);`. The docs say this prefixes "all Tailwind-generated classes and CSS variables" (`styling-with-utility-classes.mdx`, "Managing style conflicts › Using the prefix option", lines 992–1020).
- **What it generates:** your `@theme` keeps unprefixed names such as `--color-avocado-100`. The output becomes `--tw-color-avocado-100`, "to avoid conflicts with any existing variables in your project" (`upgrade-guide.mdx`, "Changes from v3 › Using a prefix", lines 590–633).
- **Cost:** class names also get the prefix, e.g. `tw:rounded-lg`. The docs show no way to prefix only the variables. You keep the built-in utilities, but your library's markup uses prefixed classes.

I didn't find anything about trimming unused built-in variables in these sections.
